q: How many brick kilns does Haryana have, what fuels do they burn and how much energy do they use?
title: Haryana brick kilns: fuel, output, energy
short: About 2,800 kilns around Jhajjar, Sonepat, Faridabad and Ambala, mostly Bull's trench kilns with some on zigzag firing, burning biomass and coal. TERI's SAMEEEKSHA page gives 14 billion bricks a year on 1.12 million toe, fired December to June.
audience: Brick kiln owners in Haryana and NCR builders asking for brick carbon figures

p: Haryana has fewer kilns than Bihar, Maharashtra or Andhra Pradesh, but each fires about 50 lakh bricks a year on about 400 toe: the largest average kiln of the four. Energy per brick is low, about 3.4 GJ per 1,000, close to Maharashtra's 3.1 and well under Bihar's 5.5.

A very few Haryana kilns make resource efficient bricks, perforated bricks and hollow blocks, alongside solid bricks. Less clay per brick means less to dry and fire. If you make them, report fuel per tonne fired as well as per brick, so a builder can compare a hollow block with the solid bricks it replaces.

ol: Coal invoices and weighbridge slips for the season.
Biomass by tonne, on its own line as biogenic.
Bricks fired by type and class, with weight per brick.
Whether the kiln fires zigzag, and since when.

example.title: An average Haryana kiln (estimate)
lines: Energy: 1.12 million toe / 2,800 = 400 toe a year
Ceiling if all coal: 400 x 41.868 GJ x 94.6 kg = about 1,580 t CO2 a year, or about 320 kg per 1,000 bricks
example.note: Totals from SAMEEEKSHA's Haryana brick page; comparisons from its pages for Bihar and Maharashtra. The ceiling uses the IPCC 2006 default for bituminous coal; biomass comes off it as biogenic.

senseible: Senseible turns a season's coal invoices into a fossil Scope 1 total, coal at 1.76 kg CO2 per kg, with each line traced to its bill for the builder who asks.
